docs.name: aase_syndrome
symptoms: Narrow shoulders ,  Droopy eyelids ,  Absent or small knuckles ,  Deformed ears ,  Pale skin ,  Triple-jointed thumbs ,  Cleft palate ,  Inability to fully extend the joints from birth
docs.description: I've been aware of some unusual physical characteristics that have been concerning me, including my narrow shoulders, droopy eyelids, and absent or small knuckles. Additionally, my ears are deformed, and my skin is quite pale. I've also noticed that I have triple-jointed thumbs, which is quite unusual. Furthermore, I was born with a cleft palate, and I've struggled with an inability to fully extend my joints since birth.

docs.name: carcinoid_syndrome
symptoms: Diarrhea ,  Difficulty breathing, such as wheezing ,  Heart problems, such as leaking heart valves, slow heartbeat, low or high blood pressure ,  Flushing (face, neck, or upper chest), or widened blood vessels seen on the skin (telangiectasias)
docs.description: I've been experiencing some distressing symptoms lately, including persistent diarrhea and difficulty breathing, which is often accompanied by wheezing. Additionally, I've been concerned about potential heart problems, such as leaking heart valves, a slow heartbeat, or abnormal blood pressure, which could be high or low. Furthermore, I've noticed some unusual physical changes, including flushing on my face, neck, or upper chest, as well as widened blood vessels visible on my skin, known as telangiectasias.

docs.name: bulimia
symptoms: Excessive exercise ,  Forcing oneself to vomit ,  Throwing away packages of laxatives, diet pills, emetics (drugs that cause vomiting), or diuretics ,  Spending a lot of time exercising ,  Suddenly eating large amounts of food or buying large amounts of food that disappear right away ,  Using laxatives, enemas, or diuretics (water pills) ,  Regularly going to the bathroom right after meals
docs.description: I've been struggling with some concerning habits lately, including excessive exercise and forcing myself to vomit, which has led me to throw away packages of laxatives, diet pills, emetics, or diuretics. I've also been spending an inordinate amount of time exercising, and I've noticed that I've been suddenly eating large amounts of food or buying large quantities that seem to disappear quickly. Furthermore, I've been relying on laxatives, enemas, or diuretics, and I've developed a habit of regularly going to the bathroom right after meals, which is causing me a lot of distress.

docs.name: apert_syndrome
symptoms: Large or late-closing soft spot on a baby's skull (fontanelle) ,  Pfeiffer syndrome ,  Webbing or fusion of the toes ,  Prominent or bulging eyes ,  Fusion or severe webbing of the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th fingers, often called "mitten hands" ,  Hearing loss ,  Short height ,  Severe under-development of the midface ,  Early closure of sutures between bones of the skull, noted by ridging along sutures (craniosynostosis) ,  Saethre-Chotzen syndrome ,  Skeletal (limb) abnormalities ,  Possible, slow intellectual development (varies from person to person) ,  Frequent ear infections ,  Carpenter syndrome (kleeblattschadel, cloverleaf skull deformity) ,  Crouzon disease (craniofacial dysostosis)
docs.description: I've been concerned about my baby's development, as I've noticed a large or late-closing soft spot on their skull, and after researching, I'm worried it might be related to a condition such as Pfeiffer syndrome or Saethre-Chotzen syndrome, which can cause a range of symptoms including webbing or fusion of the toes, prominent or bulging eyes, and fusion or severe webbing of the fingers, often referred to as "mitten hands". Additionally, I've noticed hearing loss, short height, and severe under-development of the midface, which could be related to the early closure of sutures between the bones of the skull, known as craniosynostosis. I've also been concerned about possible slow intellectual development, and my baby has been experiencing frequent ear infections. Furthermore, I've learned that these symptoms can be associated with Carpenter syndrome, also known as kleeblattschadel or cloverleaf skull deformity, or Crouzon disease, which is a type of craniofacial dysostosis.

docs.description: I've been struggling with infertility, and I've also been experiencing amenorrhea, which means I haven't been having menstrual periods. To make matters worse, I've had repeated miscarriages, and I'm not sure what's causing these issues or how to overcome them.
